tagline.text: Grassy ridge hike at the tip of the Jalajala Peninsula, ringed by Laguna de Bay

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Malaya (trailhead), Pililla, Rizal, at the tip of the Jalajala Peninsula

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~900 (per person; Manila round-trip public transport, registration and shared guide fee; food not included)

children.text: Mount Sembrano is a 745 m dormant volcano at the tip of the Jalajala Peninsula, which juts into Laguna de Bay, and its upper slopes are a treeless grassy ridge. It is about two and a half hours from Manila by public transport, which makes it a good day hike, and the summit looks out over Laguna de Bay, Talim Island, and Mount Makiling and Mount Banahaw.

Mount Sembrano is a mountain of about 745 m in the Pililla area of Rizal. Wikipedia describes it as an extinct volcano between Rizal and Laguna, about 60 km east of Manila by road. Its last eruption is thought to have been 27,000 to 29,000 years ago, so there is no volcanic activity today. A field of sulfur steam vents is said to lie at its southern tip. Wikipedia and Pinoy Mountaineer point to the same location (about 14.38° N, 121.37° E).

What makes the mountain special is its setting. It stands at the end of the Jalajala Peninsula, which pushes into Laguna de Bay, so the lake wraps around it on three sides, and together with Talim Island across the water it forms the southeastern rim of the Laguna caldera. Once you climb out of the forest onto the grassy ridge, almost nothing blocks the view. From the summit you can see Laguna de Bay, Talim Island, Mount Banahaw, Mount Makiling and the Sierra Madre, and some hiking accounts say that on very clear days even Mount Arayat is visible in the distance.

Most hikers start at the barangay hall in Barangay Malaya, Pililla. The trail begins on a concrete road and climbs gently through a mango orchard to the Manggahan campsite, then goes through a steep forest section before opening onto the grassy ridge. The first peak you reach on the ridge is the North Peak, and a little farther on is the highest point, the South Peak. A trail from Pakil on the Laguna side is also said to exist, but it is rarely used. The round-trip distance is given as about
7.5 km
to
11 km

depending on the source, and the elevation gain is about 600 m (roughly 2,000 ft). One account notes that there are restrooms and showers in the trailhead village for washing up after the hike, so ask at the barangay hall when you arrive.

The mountain was for a time a stronghold of New People's Army (NPA) insurgents, and it is said the hiking restriction was only lifted around 2012. Today it is a popular hiking spot where the barangay runs registration and guides. The mountain also has a sacred story. It is said that in 1909–1910 a carpenter found an image of the Virgin Mary in a maulawin log cut on this mountain, and some pieces are enshrined at an Aglipayan church in Santa Cruz, Laguna. A large boulder beside the trail called Simbahan (Church) is said to bear the footprints of the Virgin Mary. Think of the difficulty as a short, simple mountain with strong sun. You climb the full 745 m from sea level, and sources give anywhere from 2 to 4 hours to the summit. Many say beginners can do it, but the shadeless ridge and the slippery forest trail after rain take a lot of energy. If you leave Manila before dawn, you can be back the same day. The origin of the name Sembrano is unknown. Trail running events of 8 km, 10 km and 30 km are also said to be held here, so the trail may be crowded on race days.

blocks.title: Near-360-degree views of Laguna de Bay

children.text: From the grassy summit area the lake spreads out on three sides, followed by Talim Island, Mount Makiling and Mount Banahaw. On clear days you can even see the Sierra Madre.

blocks.title: North Peak and South Peak grassy ridge

children.text: A treeless carpet of cogon grass runs along the ridge. You pass the North Peak first, and the South Peak (745 m) is the summit. The breeze is cooling, but the grass blades can cut skin easily.
This is a rest area under mango trees, about
1–1.5 hours
after you start. It has a restroom and water, and a side trail of about 5 minutes leads to Manggahan Falls. Water flow may be low in the dry season.
Beyond the campsite, a steep forest trail full of roots and rocks follows. One hiking account reported grades of over 40%, and many say this is the hardest section.
This large boulder is said to bear the footprints of the Virgin Mary. It is a place the community regards as sacred, so please be quiet and respectful when taking photos.

blocks.title: Easy access for a day hike

children.text: Take a van from EDSA Crossing in Manila to Tanay, then transfer to a jeepney. It is one of the few Rizal mountains reachable by public transport. Many reports say you can be back in Manila around 8 PM if you leave before dawn.

blocks.title: Chance of a sea of clouds

children.text: Some sources say you can see mist lying over the lake in the early morning in winter. This comes from a promotional line in one outlet and is not guaranteed, so treat it as a better chance if you start before dawn.

items.title: Day hike route
items.subtitle: Round trip from Malaya barangay hall to the South Peak

children.text: Meet at EDSA Crossing in Manila (Starmall Shaw terminal) and board a van or UV Express to Tanay. On weekends, leave early to get a seat.
Arrive at Tanay market and transfer to a jeepney or tricycle to Malaya. The ride takes about
20–40 minutes
Have breakfast at the barangay hall, register and get your guide assigned. Bring at least
2 liters
of water.
Set off along the paved road and climb gently past farmland and the mango orchard.
Rest at the Manggahan campsite. It has a restroom and you can refill water, but it needs treatment.
Climb the steep forest section. After about
1.5–2 hours
the grassland opens up.
Pass the North Peak and reach the South Peak summit for lunch and the view.
Start the descent. After rain, going down can be harder than going up.
Return to the barangay hall to wash up and sort out your gear. The last jeepney leaves in the late evening, so don't dawdle.
These times reflect the typical flow of several hiking accounts and vary with your pace, the weather and traffic.

items.subtitle: Stop at a nearby attraction after the hike

children.text: If you finish the hike a little early, you can see the windmills at Pililla Wind Farm before heading back.
Secure transport out to Tanay before sunset.
If the hike runs late, it is safer to save the wind farm for another day.

items.title: By private car or rental car

children.text: Follow Manila East Road to Pililla, then set Malaya barangay hall in your map app and drive there. The trip takes about
1.5–2 hours
You can park beside the barangay hall, and some accounts say a parking fee is charged.
Travel from Manila airport (MNL) to EDSA Crossing and continue by the public transport route above. If you have a lot of luggage, renting a car straight from the airport is easier.
November to February is the most comfortable time. The trail is relatively dry and the temperature is lower, so the ridge is less hot, and there is a better chance of mist over the lake.

March to May is dry, but the shadeless ridge is very hot and accounts mention a risk of brush fires. From June to October the forest trail is slippery and visibility is poor, so be sure to check for typhoon news.

There is no lodging on the mountain, and a day hike is the norm. You can camp at the Manggahan campsite, but because of past reports of tent theft many write-ups recommend a day hike. Recent accounts say security has improved and that military guards are posted at the trailhead, so if you camp, follow the barangay guide's instructions.

There are sari-sari stores around the barangay hall where you can buy simple snacks and water. Nothing is sold on the mountain, so be sure to bring a packed lunch and trail food. If you want to stay overnight, lodging in Tanay or Antipolo is more practical.

You have more choices for a meal after the hike in Tanay town. Buy a light snack and a cold drink before boarding the van back. It is best to check specific shops locally, and while fresh coconut drinks are sometimes sold near the barangay hall, they are not always available.
Start early. One tip says that beginning the hike around 5:30 AM gives better light at the summit and cooler conditions.
One account says the registration desk opens at around 5 AM and closes at around 8:30 AM. Check the barangay's latest notice for current hours.
For weekends, there is advice to reserve a guide in advance through the barangay's Facebook page. Bring a valid ID.
Cogon grass cuts easily, so wear long sleeves, long pants and gloves. Gaiters help in the rainy season.
Bring a dry change of clothes for the descent; the ride back in the van is much more comfortable.
Trekking poles help on the steep forest trail and on the way down. Do some stair climbing and similar training for 4 to 6 weeks beforehand.
Carry out all your trash and do not pick plants. Also avoid loud music.
Phone signal may be weak or absent in places, so tell someone your plans in advance.
During trail running events or long weekends the registration line can be long, so aim for a weekday or a quieter weekend.
Good waterproofing is needed. Put your phone and bag in waterproof covers, and bring a raincoat in the rainy season.
The summit ridge has no shade, no water and no shelter from lightning, so if you hear thunder, head down toward the forest right away.
Water is available only at the Manggahan campsite and near the falls and needs treating, so carry 2 to 3 liters from the start.
Most write-ups say registration and a barangay guide are required. Do not climb without a guide or use unofficial steep trails.
Brush fires are a danger in the dry season, and slippery mud and slopes in the rainy season. Descending after rain is harder.
Theft of belongings from campsites has been reported, so leave valuables at home.
Registration fees, guide fees, operating hours and access rules change, so check with Barangay Malaya before you go.
A ridge of windmills in the same Pililla area, about
20–30 minutes
away by car. It is worth a stop after the hike.

blocks.title: Tanay Old Town and San Ildefonso Church

children.text: A Spanish-style church and market in Tanay town, on the way to Malaya, and a good place to eat before or after the trip.
A waterfall resort in Tanay, good for easing your muscles the day after the hike.
Another hiking route on Talim Island across Laguna de Bay. You can see it across the water from the Sembrano summit.
